caption:
Anthropic's IPO filing says that by April 2026, its own staff's Claude use was worth more each month than its personnel costs, counted at customer prices and excluding stock awards.
That internal use grew more than 250 times from January to September, and Claude now writes over 90% of the company's new code.

site_article.headline: Anthropic says its internal Claude use is now worth more than its monthly payroll
site_article.dek: The company's IPO filing values staff usage at customer prices and says Claude now writes more than 90 percent of Anthropic's new code.
site_article.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing says that by April 2026 the value of its employees' Claude use, at the prices customers pay, exceeded its monthly personnel costs excluding stock awards. That internal usage grew more than 250-fold between January and September 2026.
site_article.seo_title: Anthropic's internal Claude use now tops its monthly payroll
site_article.seo_description: Anthropic's IPO filing says staff use of Claude, valued at customer prices, passed monthly personnel costs in April 2026 and grew 250-fold this year.
site_article.answer_summary: According to its IPO filing, Anthropic's internal Claude use passed its monthly personnel costs in April 2026, but only when valued at list prices, not at what the computing actually costs the company.
site_article.hero_alt: Header image from The Cryptonomist illustrating Anthropic's internal use of Claude.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic's employees now use so much Claude that, valued at the prices the company charges customers, their usage is worth more each month than Anthropic spends on personnel. The company's IPO prospectus says that crossover happened by April 2026, measured against salaries, bonuses, benefits and contributions but not stock awards, according to The Cryptonomist and Tekedia.
The value assigned to that internal usage rose more than 250-fold between January and September 2026, the filing shows. Anthropic has about 5,300 employees, Forbes reported.

The filing also says Claude wrote more than 90 percent of the new code added to Anthropic's software in September. According to Forbes, Anthropic told investors that its engineers contributed more than 45 times as much code per day in the third quarter of 2026 as they did in 2024, and that engineers now mostly supervise coding agents rather than write code themselves.

Anthropic describes its use of Claude to research, design and develop its later models as closing the loop, Forbes reported. The company says Claude runs experiments, generates training data, automates evaluations and safety audits, and has helped find algorithmic improvements that use computing power more efficiently. Operations, sales and research staff also use teams of agents for daily work.
What the number does not show

The comparison uses retail prices, not Anthropic's actual cost of running the models. The prospectus does not disclose the real computing cost of internal usage and gives no dollar figure for the April comparison, The Cryptonomist reported. Tekedia noted that the figure does not mean Anthropic spends more cash on computing than it pays its staff.

Anthropic calls its use of Claude to build Claude a significant structural advantage, but the filing also lists risks, according to Forbes. They include AI progress outpacing safety and security measures, errors in current models carrying into later ones, and difficulty measuring the true pace of progress until a model is finished. The company also warns that rivals using AI more efficiently could leave it behind, and it proposes an industry effort to pace the frontier along with independent safety reviews of frontier models. Anthropic expects to spend $1 billion over five years with Accenture to build capacity for outside reviewers.

The disclosure is less about Anthropic's expenses than about how its work gets done. If most new code and a growing share of research tasks run through Claude, the company's output depends more on computing capacity than on headcount, which helps explain why revenue per employee is rising. It also means mistakes in one model can shape the next one, the risk Anthropic itself flags.

Watch whether Anthropic gives investors the actual computing cost of its internal Claude use before its shares begin trading, since that figure would show how much of its own capacity goes to building its next models.
